facts.fact: Neela carries a handful of lime thorns from the bush by the kitchen well, three each, for the noon signal; Devan pricks his thumb on the leopard tooth he wears on a cord at his chest.
facts.why: needed because the beat specifies a thorn and the tooth as the noon signal; the thorn source and the tooth worn on a cord are small details.

facts.fact: Neela has six pinches of resin in a banana-leaf fold for the Kodiyur road and skips resin on the night before leaving; the last turning was five nights earlier at Nellimala.
facts.why: needed because the beat has her skipping resin to save the ration and counting the ache's cost aloud.

facts.fact: The wound-share carries warmth and pleasure as well as hurt on the night they are together; a love bite leaves a matching mark on the other and they practise treating it as not a summons.
facts.why: needed because the beat requires the share to carry warmth and a practice of trusting pain is not a summons (consistent with F653, F726).

facts.fact: Devan hands Neela a warm cloth and a leaf packet of cold rice and curd at the departure.
facts.why: responsive-care beat at dawn; echoes the dawn cloth routine.

facts.fact: The corridor lamp outside the guest-room door is a plain clay lamp on a hook by the stair, found lit and filled with sesame oil at the middle watch; the left forearm welt rises an hour down the hill road.
facts.why: needed because the beat specifies the lamp refilled by Janu and the dawn welt.
